findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the ice machine baffles to have visible mold accumulation. PIC was informed that these baffles directly contact ice, which poses a cross-contamination concern. A follow-up will be conducted on September 14, 2026 to ensure the ice machine has been deep cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: There were no hanging thermometers present in all the cooling units. The PIC was informed that these devices are important in measuring and acquiring real time temperature in the units. The PIC told inspector that the thermometer will be ordered and placed in the various units respectively. Ensure that the thermometers are provided and placed within the units as discussed.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspector observed employee personal food stored amongst other food items within the standing cooler on the right side of the fryers. Education was provided and the food items in question were tossed. Ensure that there is a designated area for employees in the cooling unit (s) to avoid possible cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a leak in the plumbing of the sink compartments at the bar. A discussion about the sink was held and PIC informed inspector that these leak was previously fixed however, the leakage resumed. Hence, there is a work order for another technician to repair the sink. Ensure that the relevant plumbing repairs are done to be in compliance with the LAW.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: An accumulation of grease and food debris was observed underneath the grill and the fryers. PIC was made aware. Ensure that the accumulation is cleaned providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the mop bucket filled with used mop water in the utility sink. Discussed with the PIC. PIC told inspector that the water was from mopping the bathroom. The used mop water was discarded. Ensure that the water is disposed properly after mopping at all times.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.15 Cleaning Maintenance Tools, Preventing Contamination. FOOD preparation sinks, HANDWASHING SINKS, and WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed ice and a dark beverage in the kitchen hand sink. The PIC was informed that hand sinks cannot be used for dumping drinks. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for handwashing only and a utility sink is used for dumping drinks. The sink was rinsed and sanitized during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hand sink in the kitchen to have no available soap or paper towel for proper handwashing. The PIC was informed that proper handwashing is vital for safe food handling. The hand sink was supplied during the inspection. Ensure hand sinks are properly supplied at all times to prevent cross-contamination and food-borne illness transmission.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed no sanitizer in use at facility at time of arrival. PIC was asked to make a sanitizer bucket during the inspection, which tested 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer buckets are prepared at all times of food preparation and service to promote proper cleaning practices.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed house flies present in the kitchen near the triple sink. There was a bin of soiled wash cloths stored on the floor which seemed to be attracting the flies. Inspector suggests sealing soiled cloths in bags each night to prevent pest development. 

Inspector also observed a small swarm of gnats/drain flies present underneath the bar near the hand sink. The floors were damp and heavily soiled, which may be contributing to pest development. See violation #55 for floor cleaning details. 

A follow-up will be conducted on September 9th, 2025 to ensure the presence of pests has reduced and professional pest control has been conducted in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.citation_text: 4-204.11 Ventilation Hood Systems, Drip Prevention. Exhaust ventilation hood systems in FOOD preparation and WAREWASHING areas including components such as hoods, fans, guards, and ducting shall be designed to prevent grease or condensation from draining or dripping onto FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.comment:
Observed container of cheese sauce on steam table to measure at a temperature of 100F. Container was placed on stove top and reheated to 165F. 

3-403.11: (A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) (C) Commercially processed FOOD shall be reheated to 135F. (P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) (E) Unsliced portions of MEAT roasts may be reheated according to oven parameters and minimum TCS conditions. (C)
